Compiler owns Program lifespan.

evidence.functional_path: C03 PROVISIONAL ownership subgraph: Compiler creates Program and source buffer -> Parser appends Program AST nodes via ID-based arenas, including deep-owned CALL overflow -> AST verifier and FunctionBody owner validation -> cast_normalization builds a separate expression arena and old-to-new IDs, privately copies CALL overflow, validates external expression-ID rewrites, commits new arena only if successful and frees old overflow; failure frees uncommitted scratch -> inline specialization may still change AST -> CoreSet is published -> Compiler destroys Program and source buffer before Target backend. Distinguish borrowed element pointer lifetimes, source IDs, dynamic call-site specialization facts, and physical ownership.
limitations: MAPPING_PROPOSED ONLY. Sampled C03 source and existing canonical design documentation; not all callers, failure paths, AST node variants, transformations or platform tests audited.

Check nested Program/Parser realloc borrow invalidation through parser_expression, GNU static_initializer and inline clone paths; historical MC-001..MC-009/MC-023/MC-030 require source-current cross-check.
Check cast normalization corner cases: prevalidation versus external Program mutation, original owned overflow and rollback on allocation/invalid edge, exact AST stage/FunctionBody contracts.
Shallow MinicParser snapshots used only for lexical probes may be legitimate; copying ownership before semantic parsing cannot be labeled unsafe without write trace and real counterexample.
